result.topic_en: The page gives the partial-fraction decomposition (logarithm and arctangent terms) of the integral of x^{m-1}dx/(1+x^k), and then evaluates the integral of dp/(1-p^4)^{1/4} through the substitution 1-p^4 = p^4 x^4, with a numerical example at p = 0.8.
result.transcription:
$\int\frac{x^{m-1}dx}{(1+x)^{k})^{n}}$ =
$-\frac{2}{k}\cos\frac{m\pi}{k}\, l\sqrt{(1-2x\cos\frac{\pi}{k}+xx)}$
$-\frac{2}{k}\cos\frac{3m\pi}{k}\, l\sqrt{(1-2x\cos\frac{3\pi}{k}+xx)}$
$-$ &c
$-\frac{2}{k}\cos\frac{im\pi}{k}\, l\sqrt{(1-2x\cos\frac{i\pi}{k}+xx)}$
$+\frac{2}{k}\sin\frac{m\pi}{k}\, A.tg\,\frac{x\sin\frac{\pi}{k}}{1-x\cos\frac{\pi}{k}}$
$+\frac{2}{k}\sin\frac{3m\pi}{k}\, A.tg\,\frac{x\sin\frac{3\pi}{k}}{1-x\cos\frac{3\pi}{k}}$
$+$ &c

$\int\frac{dp}{\sqrt[4]{(1-p^4)}}$ = (posito $1-p^4=p^4x^4$)
$\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}}\, l\,\frac{1-x\sqrt{2}+xx}{1+x\sqrt{2}+xx}$ $x=\sqrt[4]{\frac{1-p^4}{p^4}}$
$+\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}}\, A.tg.\,\frac{x\sqrt{2}}{1-xx}$ $=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}}\, A.\cos$ [-$\frac{1+xx}{(1+xx)^2}$-] [?] $\frac{(1-xx)^2}{1+x^4}$
Also $x=0$ | $0$
$x=\infty$ | [-...-]
Also für [?] $p=0{,}8$
$x=\sqrt[4]{\frac{5904}{4096}}$

methods.what: Partial-fraction decomposition of the integral of x^{m-1}/(1+x^k) into logarithm and arctangent terms over the odd multiples of pi/k
Arctangent terms of the same decomposition
Substitution 1-p^4 = p^4 x^4 to rationalize the integral of dp/(1-p^4)^{1/4}
Closed form of the integral of dp/(1-p^4)^{1/4} in logarithms and an arctangent
Rewriting the arctangent term as an arccosine
